events.title: A stone from the night sky

secrets.clue: A page under a loose stone. The old makers drew a wheel that drinks the wind.
The frame hums when the lane is quiet. Nobody left a name on it.

money.bond: owes a kindness at the oven

lines.speaker: kura_rasho
lines.text: The loaf is still round. A coin has corners. I am only saying.

lines.speaker: dayka_hapsa
lines.text: And the coin is gone, and the loaf is here. Carry it before you count the corners.

money.life: carrying a small debt and a jug
money.routine: sets a little aside each evening

lines.speaker: pura_shrin
lines.text: The coin can sit until the jug comes home. That is the whole bargain.

lines.speaker: dayka_hapsa
lines.text: Then the jug may travel, and nobody has to make a speech about it.

money.life: a loaf she did not have to ask for

lines.speaker: nabata_bchuk
lines.text: There is a loaf and no argument attached. I checked.

lines.speaker: kcha_zenab
lines.text: Then we eat the middle first. The heel can be the argument tomorrow.

lines.speaker: pira_majid
lines.text: The boy has one jar to carry at dawn. Not a lecture.

lines.speaker: kura_rasho
lines.text: Two jars, if the well is closer than he counted. I stepped it.

lines_rich.speaker: fata_chawpes
lines_rich.text: The asking price sat down this week. The lane feels lighter.

lines_rich.speaker: khana_nasre
lines_rich.text: Then we can finish the hem. Nobody is poorer for a fair price.

lines_poor.speaker: fata_chawpes
lines_poor.text: The asking price stood up. Keep the good thread in the basket.

lines_poor.speaker: khana_nasre
lines_poor.text: We will mend what we have. A dear week is not a disaster.

side_quests.title: Questions at supper
side_quests.summary: A bright child keeps asking how the relic frame fits together. The parents answer with supper. The grandmother asks him to carry the bread first.

side_quests.title: The round loaf
side_quests.summary: A boy explains that a round loaf should cost less because it has no corners. His mother tells him to carry it.

side_quests.title: The borrowed jug
side_quests.summary: An aunt will lend the good jug if a coin waits for it. The bargain is quieter than the boy expected.

side_quests.title: One jar at dawn
side_quests.summary: An elder hires a boy to carry one jar. The boy has already counted the steps and wants to carry two.

side_quests.title: The queue for nails
side_quests.summary: A chalk list on a broken post says who may take two nails. The list is older than the people waiting. They laugh, then they wait anyway.
side_quests.limits: no gore, no sexual content, almost no swearing
